questions.q: On a picklist's Values related list, what does the Replace button do?
options: Deletes the picklist field entirely
Bulk-swaps every record currently holding one value over to a different value
Reorders the picklist's values alphabetically
Converts the picklist into a global value set automatically
questions.explain: Replace lets you swap every record currently holding one value over to a different value in bulk, without hand-editing each record.

questions.q: In a field dependency between Issue Type and Issue Detail, which role does Issue Type play?
options: The dependent field, filtered by Issue Detail
The controlling field — what the user picks first, filtering Issue Detail's options
Neither; Issue Type is unrelated to the dependency
A global value set shared across objects
questions.explain: The lesson's example sets Issue Type as the controlling field and Issue Detail as the dependent field whose values get filtered.

questions.q: On the field dependency's filter-rules grid, what do the columns and rows represent?
options: Columns are user profiles, rows are page layouts
Columns are controlling-field values, rows are dependent-field values, with checkboxes at each intersection
Columns are objects, rows are record types
Columns are fiscal years, rows are currencies
questions.explain: The grid places controlling-field values as columns and dependent-field values as rows, and Include Values/Exclude Values sets the checkbox at each intersection.

questions.q: What field types can serve as a dependent field in a field dependency?
options: Any field type, including text and number fields
Custom picklists and multi-select picklists
Only standard checkboxes
Only lookup fields
questions.explain: The lesson states that custom picklists and multi-select picklists can be dependent fields (while standard/custom checkboxes and picklists under 300 values can be controlling fields).

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a dependent picklist prevents bad data more reliably than training users on valid combinations?
options: Because it makes the wrong combination unselectable in the UI itself, before the record is ever saved — not dependent on a user remembering a rule
Because it automatically emails an admin whenever a user makes a mistake
Because it deletes any record with an invalid combination after the fact
Because training is never effective for any kind of data entry
questions.explain: The lesson frames the dependent picklist as a guardrail built into the field — the invalid option simply isn't selectable, rather than relying on a user remembering a rule or a validation rule catching it afterward.
